articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually leaked AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it was their personal diary. When the agency responsible for cybersecurity can't secure their own cloud credentials, you know we're living in the best timeline.

articles.title: Coinflow CISO on crypto payments security under AI pressure
articles.summary: LiteSpeed cPanel plugin zero-day got weaponized for root-level script execution in the wild. CISA's emergency patching order proves someone's having a very bad week in hosting land.

articles.title: Cybersecurity Evolution: How We Went From Perimeter Defense to AI-Native Security
articles.summary: AI is now writing exploits faster than security scanners can detect them, proving that artificial intelligence has finally achieved human-level laziness. The robots aren't coming for our jobs—they're coming for our vulnerabilities.

articles.title: The 60/40 portfolio’s glaring weakness
articles.summary: CrowdStrike and Google tag-teamed GlassWorm malware targeting developers through poisoned packages. Supply chain attacks remain the gift that keeps on giving to anyone who trusts random npm modules.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: Police are using license plate readers for everything from school residency checks to noise complaints because mission creep is the only constant in surveillance tech. Your commute is now a perpetual background check.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a rare win for end-to-end encryption in a world determined to make our digital conversations as private as a megaphone in Times Square. Encrypted messaging survives another regulatory assault.

articles.title: 5 Steps to Managing Shadow AI Tools Without Slowing Down Employees
articles.summary: Malicious npm package specifically targeted Claude AI users' data directories via GitHub uploads. Even AI assistants can't escape the curse of dependency hell and sketchy package managers.

articles.title: India's cyber agency sets clock at 12 hours to tackle exploited bugs as AI turns up the heat
articles.summary: Extortion crews are literally walking into law firms pretending to be tech support and plugging in USB drives like it's 2003. Social engineering remains undefeated against human gullibility.

articles.title: Tucker Carlson Doles Out Some Truly Strange Credit Card Advice
articles.summary: Indian student hacker claims to have breached CBSE exam system while the board insists it was just a 'testing platform.' Nothing says educational integrity like arguing over which system got pwned.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: Congress demands answers after CISA's spectacular AWS credential leak, because apparently oversight only kicks in after the barn door is wide open and the horses have formed their own botnet.
